title: 黄仁勋被盯上：高管却以为没机密就安全，去中国前该问哪三个问题？
speaker: Peter Mattis

segments.en: Look, I've given security awareness briefings to many corporate executives and one of the things is kind of astonishing is that a lot of people say, well, I don't have classified information,
segments.zh: 我给许多企业高管做过安全防范简报，令人惊讶的是，很多人说，我没有机密信息，

segments.en: why would I be a target? That's kind of the first thing, and I don't think it's unique, certainly not unique to Jensen Huang, and it's certainly not unique to Americans.
segments.zh: 为什么我会成为目标？这是第一个问题，我认为这并不独特，当然不是黄仁勋独有的，也肯定不是美国人独有的。

segments.en: If you haven't lived in that world, you haven't really thought about it. You think of spying as being this particular glamorous thing or that you can get after these high value precision points of
segments.zh: 如果你没有在那个世界生活过，你就没有真正想过。你认为间谍活动是某种迷人的事情，或者你可以获取这些高价值的精确信息点。

segments.en: information. Sometimes you can, but that's not always helped. The second thing is that I think a lot of people think of security and personal protection, and personal protection is one thing,
segments.zh: 有时你可以，但并非总是有帮助。第二件事是，我认为很多人想到安全和人身保护，人身保护是一回事，

segments.en: but that's not what this is. The third, I think a lot of people just don't have the recognition of questions that they should be asking about individuals or thinking about what might be used against
segments.zh: 但这不是这个。第三，我认为很多人只是没有意识到他们应该问的关于个人的问题，或者思考什么可能被用来对付他们。

segments.en: them. Give us a few examples of that. Give us a few of those tools. What should executives who may be watching wonder about or the questions that they should be asking if they go to China?
segments.zh: 给我们举几个例子。给我们一些工具。可能观看的高管们应该想知道什么，或者如果他们去中国，应该问什么问题？
